items.definition: A coiled brass instrument whose valves redirect air through a long tube.
A large brass instrument that produces low notes through a wide, conical bore.
A compact brass instrument with valves and a rounded, conical tube.
A mellow-sounding brass instrument with valves and a broad, conical bore.
A simple brass instrument that plays notes from the natural harmonic series.
A medium-sized brass instrument with valves and a warm, low register.
A large circular brass instrument designed to be carried around the player's body.
A brass instrument with valves, commonly used to play middle harmonies in marching bands.
A slender woodwind instrument that produces sound when air is blown across an opening.
A woodwind instrument with a single reed, a cylindrical body, and a wide range.
A single-reed woodwind instrument with a curved metal body and a flared bell.
A woodwind instrument with two reeds and a bright, penetrating tone.
A large double-reed woodwind instrument that plays in a low register.
A simple flute-like woodwind instrument with a whistle mouthpiece and finger holes.
A small handheld instrument that sounds when breath passes across internal metal reeds.
A wind instrument that uses an air bag to supply several pipes continuously.
A keyboard instrument whose keys cause hammers to strike stretched strings.
A small bowed string instrument, typically played beneath the player's chin.
A bowed string instrument held between the knees and played in a low register.
A fretted string instrument, usually played by plucking or strumming its strings.
A large string instrument with strings stretched across a frame and plucked by hand.
A percussion instrument that makes sound when a stretched membrane or surface is struck.
A percussion instrument with tuned wooden bars struck using small mallets.
A plucked string instrument with a long neck and a round, drumlike body.
A removable fitting that directs a player's breath into a brass instrument.
A small device inserted into a brass instrument to reduce its volume during practice.
A light lubricant used to keep moving brass-instrument valves working smoothly.
A protective container with a handle or straps for transporting a musical instrument.
A folding support that holds printed music at a convenient reading height.
Printed notation that records pitches, rhythms, and instructions for performers.
A slender stick used to mark tempo and communicate musical cues to performers.
A large indoor venue designed for audiences to hear live musical performances.
A human-powered vehicle with two wheels, pedals, and a steering handlebar.
A very large land mammal with a trunk, broad ears, and thick legs.
An intelligent marine mammal with a streamlined body and a long, narrow snout.
An insect with four broad, often colorful wings and a coiled feeding tube.
A round, edible fruit with crisp flesh and a central core containing seeds.
A long upholstered seat designed to accommodate several people.
A long-lived tree with lobed leaves and acorns that serve as its seeds.
A curved band of colors formed when sunlight is refracted and reflected by water droplets.
